Negative binomial regression

nbreg.Rd

Fits a negative binomial (NB2) regression model with log link, similar to MASS::glm.nb(). The coefficients are estimated by iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) and the dispersion parameter theta by Newton-Raphson on the log scale; the two steps are alternated until the log-likelihood converges. No general-purpose optimizer is used.

Usage

nbreg(formula, data, offset, control = nbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A model formula such as y ~ x1 + x2. An offset can be included as offset(log(exposure)).

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

An optional numeric vector with an offset on the log scale (for example log(exposure)).

control

A list of control parameters from nbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "nbreg": a list containing

coefficients

Estimated regression coefficients.

vcov

Variance-covariance matrix of the coefficients.

theta

Estimated dispersion parameter.

SE.theta

Standard error of theta.

loglik

Log-likelihood at the estimates.

iterations

Number of outer iterations used.

converged

TRUE if the algorithm converged.

fitted.values

Fitted means.

linear.predictors

Linear predictor, including the offset.

call

The matched call.

together with the response y, the offset, the model frame model, the terms, and the numbers n and df.residual.

Details

The model is \(E(Y_i) = \mu_i\), \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top \beta + o_i\) and \(Var(Y_i) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2 / \theta\), where \(o_i\) is an optional offset. Standard errors of the coefficients come from \((X^\top \hat{W} X)^{-1}\) with theta treated as known, as in MASS::glm.nb().

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- rnorm(200)
y <- rnbinom(200, size = 2, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.8 * x))
d <- data.frame(y = y, x = x)

fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = d)
fit$coefficients
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.5264662   0.7583828 
fit$theta
#> [1] 2.060895
